subject.title: fix(tool-call-repair): parse JSON-format plain-text tool calls alongside bracket/XML/Harmony

question: Should providers using `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper` interpret validated JSON objects in assistant text as executable tool calls, rather than limiting repair to the existing bracket, XML, and Harmony grammars?
rationale: This changes the trusted interpretation of model-authored text across multiple providers and cannot be settled by tests alone; maintainers must confirm that the compatibility wrapper owns this executable grammar and its false-positive tradeoff.

options.title: Approve wrapper-level JSON repair
options.body: Keep the shared parser for providers that explicitly opt into the compatibility wrapper, require exact-path live proof, and leave native Ollama structured-call handling tracked separately.

options.title: Require provider-local opt-in
options.body: Expose a generic JSON parser capability but require each provider wrapper to enable it explicitly so existing compatibility behavior does not broaden automatically.

options.title: Decline JSON execution fallback
options.body: Limit repair to current grammars and fix each provider's native structured tool-call normalization instead of executing JSON found in text.

recommendation.title: Approve wrapper-level JSON repair
recommendation.body: Keep the shared parser for providers that explicitly opt into the compatibility wrapper, require exact-path live proof, and leave native Ollama structured-call handling tracked separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The behavior originates in the shared repair package introduced by this owner, making them the strongest available routing candidate for the permanent compatibility boundary.
